reference: Fixed documented xattr/POSIX contracts plus Python os.setxattr/getxattr/listxattr independent API comparisons on private user.* files. No claim of GNU getfattr/setfattr CLI parity.
coverage: Bash builtin registration and help metadata
user namespace attribute write/read, including a zero-length value and -V binding
XATTR_CREATE and XATTR_REPLACE write flags, including conflict failure and unchanged old value
list variable contents with order-insensitive assertion
-F descriptor write/read and -L no-follow read against an attributed target
Python API interoperability for binary reads and independently inspected writes; not GNU CLI parity.
exclusions: The read ERANGE retry loop needs a deterministic concurrent-writer syscall fixture or mock; this suite does not introduce a timing race.
Security namespaces, privileged ownership changes, and filesystem-wide xattr capability behavior are outside the private user.* file fixtures.

cases.purpose: Confirm xattr is registered as a Bash builtin and its help metadata is available, without counting this as operation coverage.
cases.script:
trap 'rm -f discard.out' EXIT
[[ $(type -t xattr) == builtin ]]
help xattr >discard.out
printf 'builtin\nhelp-ok\n'

cases.purpose: Write and read a user.* value containing a space; the documented syscall wrapper returns the value bytes unchanged.
cases.script:
: > note
xattr write note user.note 'hello shell'
xattr read note user.note
printf '\n'

cases.purpose: Exercise a valid zero-byte xattr value and distinguish it from command output using fixed delimiters.
cases.script:
: > empty-value
xattr write empty-value user.empty ''
printf 'before<'
xattr read empty-value user.empty
printf '>after\n'

cases.purpose: Check the documented read -V binding path with a simple value that is representable in a Bash variable.
cases.script:
: > variable-value
xattr write variable-value user.value 'kept value'
xattr read variable-value user.value -V got
printf '<%s>\n' "$got"

cases.purpose: Check that create initializes an absent name and replace updates an existing name, as defined by XATTR_CREATE and XATTR_REPLACE.
cases.script:
: > flagged
xattr write flagged user.state first -f create
xattr write flagged user.state second -f replace
xattr read flagged user.state
printf '\n'

cases.purpose: Require create-on-existing to fail with command status 1 and leave the prior attribute value intact.
cases.script:
: > conflict
xattr write conflict user.state preserved
rc=0
xattr write conflict user.state rejected -f create || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
xattr read conflict user.state
printf '\nwrite-status=%d\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Check newline-separated list -V binding while accepting either kernel enumeration order for the two names.
cases.script:
: > names
xattr write names user.alpha a
xattr write names user.beta b
xattr list names -V attrs
case ${attrs//$'\n'/|} in
  'user.alpha|user.beta'|'user.beta|user.alpha') printf 'two names present\n' ;;
  *) exit 2 ;;
esac

cases.purpose: Remove an existing value, then verify a read of the missing name fails with status 1.
cases.script:
: > removable
xattr write removable user.gone value
xattr remove removable user.gone
rc=0
xattr read removable user.gone || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
printf 'removed; absent-read-status=%d\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Descriptor mode replaces the PATH operand. Independently cross-check descriptor writes with path reads and path writes with descriptor reads.
cases.script:
: > fd-file
exec {xattr_fd}<>fd-file
xattr -F "$xattr_fd" write user.fd 'via descriptor'
xattr read fd-file user.fd
printf '\n'
xattr write fd-file user.fd 'via path'
xattr -F "$xattr_fd" read user.fd
printf '\n'
exec {xattr_fd}>&-

cases.purpose: Verify -L read does not follow a symlink to an attributed target: the link read must fail while a normal target read still returns the stored value.
cases.script:
: > target
ln -s target link
xattr write target user.marker target-value
rc=0
xattr -L read link user.marker || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]]
xattr read target user.marker
printf '\nlink-read-status=%d\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Qualify the documented read retry path when an attribute grows between the size probe and data read.
cases.reason: Argument matching in a stateless filter is enough for the retry and exhaustion paths, so no mock driver is needed for them. Only a probe that changes between calls needs a stateful supervisor.

cases.purpose: Descriptor list and remove omit PATH and operate on an independently opened private fixture.
cases.script:
: > fd-file
exec {fd}<>fd-file
xattr -F "$fd" write user.one value
xattr -F "$fd" list -V keys
[[ $keys == user.one ]]
xattr -F "$fd" remove user.one
xattr list fd-file -V remaining
[[ -z $remaining ]]
xattr -F "$fd" list
exec {fd}>&-

cases.purpose: Read an independently seeded NUL/high-bit user attribute and compare raw bytes against Python os.getxattr.
cases.script:
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
import os
open('binary-value','wb').close()
os.setxattr('binary-value','user.binary',b'A\0B\xff')
PYC
if [[ $(type -t xattr) == builtin ]]; then
 xattr read binary-value user.binary
else
 python3 -c 'import os,sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(os.getxattr("binary-value","user.binary"))'
fi

cases.purpose: Independently inspect candidate-written attribute bytes and names with Python; this checks actual xattrs, which are absent from harness tree snapshots.
cases.script:
printf payload > target
if [[ $(type -t xattr) == builtin ]]; then
 xattr write target user.value 'spaces and text'
else
 python3 -c 'import os; os.setxattr("target","user.value",b"spaces and text")'
fi
PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 - <<'PYC'
import os,sys
sys.stdout.buffer.write(os.getxattr('target','user.value'))
print()
print(','.join(sorted(os.listxattr('target'))))
PYC

cases.purpose: XATTR_REPLACE must fail for an absent attribute.
cases.script:
: > target
xattr write target user.absent value -f replace
